title: Titila, the Shy Shooting Star
summary: Titila is a shooting star so shy that she never dares to cross the sky. She's afraid of getting children's wishes wrong.

scenes.text:
High up in the night lived a very small shooting star. Her name was Titila.

Every night, the other shooting stars flew across the sky from end to end, leaving golden tails behind them. And down below, in their beds, children watched them go by and made wishes.

They all went. All except Titila.

Titila stayed hidden behind a big, fat, white cloud. From there she looked at the sleeping world: the rooftops, the rivers, the lit-up windows.

And she shone very softly, twinkling, so that nobody would see her.

Why didn't she cross?

Because she was scared.

"What if a child wishes for a hug and I bring them a balloon?" she thought. "What if they wish for a puppy and I bring them a duck? What if I get the wish wrong?"

Just thinking about it made her hide even further behind the cloud.

Until the cloud spoke.

"Excuse me," it said, in a soft, squashy voice. "Could you move over a bit? You're tickling me."

Titila went red. Well, more yellow.

"Sorry. I'm hiding."

"I know," said the cloud, with a fluffy giggle. "You've been hiding behind me for three weeks. My name's Cotton."

"And what are you hiding from?" asked Cotton.

Titila told him about her fear. The hug and the balloon. The puppy and the duck.

Cotton thought about it, which for a cloud is like a slow stretch.

"Titila," he said. "You don't grant wishes."

"I don't?"

"No. You just go by, and shine. Each child brings their own wish, and keeps it in their heart. You're the light that helps them make it."

Titila thought about it for a long time.

"So… I can't get it wrong?"

"Nobody gets it wrong by shining," said Cotton. "Look. I'll move over a little, and you just peek out. All right?"

Cotton moved over a little.

And Titila peeked out.

Down below, at a window, there was a girl who couldn't get to sleep. She was sitting up in bed, hugging her knees, looking at the sky. As if she were waiting for something.

Titila felt all her light tremble.

She took one very deep breath.

And she crossed.

From one end of the sky to the other, leaving a golden tail behind her, long and soft.

Down below, the girl opened her eyes very wide. Then she closed them, put her hands together, and made a wish in a tiny voice.

Titila never found out what the wish was.

But she saw that the girl was smiling. That she snuggled down under her blanket. And that she fell asleep, peacefully, with the smile still on.

And she understood that she didn't need to know.

She went slowly back to her corner of the sky, where Cotton was waiting.

"Well?" asked the cloud.

"Again tomorrow," said Titila.

And that night, for the first time, she shone without hiding.
